Where To Work planning units for an area of interest

Source: R/wtw.R
create_wtw_planning_units.Rd

Makes the 1 km planning units of an area of interest (AOI) for a Where To Work (WTW) project, and writes the project's AOI and planning-unit files: create_1km_grid() on a NAT_DATA folder (ConsTech's shared national data), then, with project_dir, aoi/aoi.shp, aoi/pu_1km.shp and aoi/pu_1km.tif. It is wtw-data-prep2's step 02 in one call, and the defaults write the files that step writes.

Usage

create_wtw_planning_units(
  aoi,
  natdata_dir,
  project_dir = NULL,
  cells = "touches",
  value = "NCCID",
  id = "PUID",
  index = "template",
  order = "value",
  trim = TRUE,
  aoi_file = "aoi/aoi.shp",
  polygons_file = "aoi/pu_1km.shp",
  raster_file = "aoi/pu_1km.tif",
  raster_value = 1,
  raster_datatype = "INT1U",
  raster_name = "layer",
  overwrite = TRUE,
  template_file = "_1km/idx.tif"
)

Arguments

aoi

The AOI, one feature: anything read_aoi() accepts (sf, sfc or SpatVector polygons, a file path, or bounds with their CRS in an sf bbox), holding exactly one feature (one row, a polygon or multipolygon). An AOI of several features is an error, raised before anything is written; dissolve them first, for example with read_aoi(). Bounds are one feature, their rectangle. A file path is read with read_layer(), from the layer named as <path>/<layer> or the first layer. The AOI is read once into memory before anything is written, so it can be the aoi_file this call overwrites.

natdata_dir

The NAT_DATA folder: a single path to an existing folder, such as a dated release (NAT_DATA_20261009). Its template, the file template_file, is opened with natdata_template(). Where NAT_DATA lives is each tool's own setting; this function only reads from it.

project_dir

The WTW project folder: NULL (the default) writes nothing, or a single folder path, under which the files named by aoi_file, polygons_file and raster_file are written. Missing folders, project_dir included, are created. Where the project lives is each tool's own setting.

cells

The cell inclusion rule, one of "touches" (every cell the AOI touches) or "centre" (every cell whose centre is inside the AOI). The default, "touches", gives the cells wtw-data-prep2 gives.

value

The name of the column of national IDs in the polygons, and of the raster's layer: a single, non-empty string. The default, "NCCID", is NAT_DATA's name.

id

NULL or the name of a column that numbers the polygons 1 to n in their order (see order): a single, non-empty string, different from value. The default, "PUID", is the planning-unit ID of Where To Work projects. NULL adds none.

index

What the national ID (value) is, one of:

  • "template" (the default): the template's value in each cell. In NAT_DATA, _1km/idx.tif numbers its cells row by row from the bottom-left cell; this is the shared national ID that wtw-data-prep2 writes as NCCID and other tools join on.

  • "cell": the cell's number in the template in terra's numbering (row by row from the top-left cell, starting at 1), which links each cell directly to the columns of NAT_DATA's rij matrices.

order

The order of the polygons, and so of id, one of:

  • "value" (the default): sorted by national ID (value), smallest first, as wtw-data-prep2 orders them.

  • "cell": terra's cell order (row by row from the top-left cell), as polygonize_raster() returns them.

With index = "cell" the two orders are the same.

trim

A single logical, the extent of the returned raster and of raster_file:

  • TRUE (the default): trimmed to the planning-unit cells, the extent of wtw-data-prep2's pu_1km.tif. Edge rows and columns of the AOI's box that have no planning units are removed.

  • FALSE: the AOI's bounding box on the template's grid, as create_1km_grid() returns it.

The two differ only when an edge row or column of the AOI's box has no template data, for example on a coast or at the edge of the national data.

aoi_file, polygons_file, raster_file

The files to write, as paths relative to project_dir, or NULL to not write that file:

  • aoi_file: the AOI's one feature with its attributes, reprojected to the template's CRS, as wtw-data-prep2 writes aoi.shp. Default "aoi/aoi.shp".

  • polygons_file: the planning-unit polygons. Default "aoi/pu_1km.shp".

  • raster_file: the planning-unit raster, raster_value in every planning unit. Default "aoi/pu_1km.tif".

The defaults are the WTW project layout wtw-data-prep2 writes. The vector files' format follows their extension (any format GDAL writes, such as .shp or .gpkg); raster_file is written by write_rasters(). The three must be different files.

raster_value

A single finite number, the value of the planning units in raster_file. The default, 1, is wtw-data-prep2's. Ignored without raster_file.

raster_datatype

The data type of raster_file, one of terra's data types (see terra::writeRaster()). The default, "INT1U", is wtw-data-prep2's. raster_value must be a value it stores: for an integer type, a whole number after rounding (halves away from zero) within the type's range and not its NoData value (for example 0 to 254 for "INT1U"). Ignored without raster_file.

raster_name

A single, non-empty string, the name of the one band (layer) of raster_file, as terra reads it back with names(). The default, "layer", is wtw-data-prep2's. Ignored without raster_file.

overwrite

A single logical. TRUE (the default) replaces existing files, as wtw-data-prep2 does; FALSE is an error if any of the files exists, checked before any file is written.

template_file

The template's file within natdata_dir, as a path relative to it, passed to natdata_template() as its file. The default, "_1km/idx.tif", is NAT_DATA's national template. Another path opens a template kept elsewhere in the folder, such as another version or resolution of the grid.

Value

The list create_1km_grid() returns, differing from it only in the raster's extent (see trim):

  • aoi: the AOI dissolved into one polygon, an sf data frame without attributes, in the template's CRS;

  • aoi_raster: a SpatRaster with one layer named value, on the template's grid: the national ID in the planning units and NA elsewhere. It can be passed as the aoi_raster of extract_layers() and clip_rij_matrix();

  • polygons: an sf data frame with one POLYGON row per planning unit, with the columns value, id (unless id = NULL) and geometry.

With project_dir, the files named by aoi_file, polygons_file and raster_file are written as a side effect.

Method

  1. AOI: read once, with read_aoi()'s input handling and checks (polygons or multipolygons only, with a CRS), files with read_layer(); Z and M dropped; reprojected to the template's CRS (template_file in natdata_dir, by default _1km/idx.tif, in Canada_Albers_WGS_1984) with sf::st_transform() (PROJ), which moves each vertex. It must be one feature, or the function stops before anything is written; nothing is dissolved silently.

  2. Planning units: create_1km_grid() on that feature, with cells, value, id, index, order and template_file (its Method section has the details): the AOI dissolved by read_aoi() (one feature, so the same area); its cells on the template by raster intersection ("touches" is GDAL's all-touched rule), without the cells where the template is NA; one 1 km square polygon per cell, holding its national ID (NCCID) and planning-unit number (PUID).

  3. Extent: with trim = TRUE, the raster is trimmed with terra::trim() to the smallest box of whole cells holding every planning unit. If the AOI gets no cells, it is not trimmed (and create_1km_grid() warns).

  4. Writing (only with project_dir), in this order, with sf::st_write() for the vector files (an existing file's layer is replaced) and write_rasters() for the raster:

    • aoi_file: the AOI's one feature from step 1, with its attributes;

    • polygons_file: the polygons, with the columns value, id and their geometry. value keeps the type it has in the polygons, so with NAT_DATA's idx.tif (an INT* data type) NCCID is an integer field (ADR 0019);

    • raster_file: the raster of step 3 with raster_value in every planning unit and NA elsewhere, one layer named raster_name, in raster_datatype, NA as terra's NoData value for it (rounded halves away from zero before an integer type). The defaults, 1 as INT1U (NoData 255) in a layer named layer, are wtw-data-prep2's pu_1km.tif.

No areas are computed and no values are rounded. With the defaults, the files are those of wtw-data-prep2's step 02 (aoi_to_grid()): the same AOI feature and attributes, the same planning units (NCCID, PUID and polygons, with NCCID and PUID as integer fields), and the same pu_1km.tif extent, values and data type. Decisions are recorded in ADR 0017, ADR 0018, ADR 0019 and ADR 0026.

Arguments are checked before the AOI is read; the AOI is read before anything is written. If writing fails partway, the files already written are kept.

See also

create_1km_grid(), which makes the planning units, and write_rasters(), which writes the raster.

Other wtw: create_dataprep_template(), create_wtw_project_folder(), dataprep_columns(), extract_wtw_natdata(), wtw_project_folders()

Examples

# A small NAT_DATA-like folder: its _1km/idx.tif is a 10 x 10 template
natdata_dir <- system.file("extdata", "natdata", package = "constechr")
aoi <- system.file("extdata", "aoi.gpkg", package = "constechr")

# The planning units, without writing anything
pu <- create_wtw_planning_units(aoi, natdata_dir)
pu$polygons
#> Simple feature collection with 9 features and 2 fields
#> Geometry type: POLYGON
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 1003000 ymin: 604000 xmax: 1006000 ymax: 607000
#> Projected CRS: Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#>   NCCID PUID                       geometry
#> 1    34    1 POLYGON ((1003000 606000, 1...
#> 2    35    2 POLYGON ((1004000 606000, 1...
#> 3    36    3 POLYGON ((1005000 606000, 1...
#> 4    44    4 POLYGON ((1003000 605000, 1...
#> 5    45    5 POLYGON ((1004000 605000, 1...
#> 6    46    6 POLYGON ((1005000 605000, 1...
#> 7    54    7 POLYGON ((1003000 604000, 1...
#> 8    55    8 POLYGON ((1004000 604000, 1...
#> 9    56    9 POLYGON ((1005000 604000, 1...

# Write the WTW project's aoi/aoi.shp, aoi/pu_1km.shp and aoi/pu_1km.tif
project_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "wtw_project")
pu <- create_wtw_planning_units(aoi, natdata_dir, project_dir)
list.files(file.path(project_dir, "aoi"))
#> [1] "aoi.dbf"    "aoi.prj"    "aoi.shp"    "aoi.shx"    "pu_1km.dbf"
#> [6] "pu_1km.prj" "pu_1km.shp" "pu_1km.shx" "pu_1km.tif"
terra::rast(file.path(project_dir, "aoi", "pu_1km.tif"))
#> class       : SpatRaster
#> size        : 3, 3, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
#> resolution  : 1000, 1000  (x, y)
#> extent      : 1003000, 1006000, 604000, 607000  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#> coord. ref. : Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#> source      : pu_1km.tif
#> name        : layer
#> min value   :     1
#> max value   :     1

# The AOI as a GeoPackage, and no raster file
pu <- create_wtw_planning_units(
  aoi, natdata_dir, project_dir,
  aoi_file = "aoi/aoi.gpkg", raster_file = NULL
)

# An AOI of several features is an error: dissolve them first
two <- rbind(read_layer(aoi), read_layer(aoi))
try(create_wtw_planning_units(two, natdata_dir))
#> Error in create_wtw_planning_units(two, natdata_dir) : 
#>   `aoi` must be one feature, not 2.
#> ℹ Dissolve the features into one first, for example with `read_aoi()`.
pu <- create_wtw_planning_units(read_aoi(two), natdata_dir)

# The planning units as 0s in a signed data type, in a band named "pu"
pu <- create_wtw_planning_units(
  aoi, natdata_dir, project_dir,
  raster_value = 0, raster_datatype = "INT2S", raster_name = "pu"
)
terra::rast(file.path(project_dir, "aoi", "pu_1km.tif"))
#> class       : SpatRaster
#> size        : 3, 3, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
#> resolution  : 1000, 1000  (x, y)
#> extent      : 1003000, 1006000, 604000, 607000  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#> coord. ref. : Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#> source      : pu_1km.tif
#> name        : pu
#> min value   :  0
#> max value   :  0
